8.en: The shadow war waged by the Inquisition often relies on subterfuge and secrecy. They are the unseen blade that strikes from the dark, piercing the God-Emperor’s foes in the weakest points of their blasphemous flesh, using surprise and guile to circumvent their vile armour. The Holy Orders abhor their odious enemies, but many Inquisitors begrudgingly treat their grotesque foes with a measure of regard for their dangerous capabilities. A wise Inquisitor knows the impossible odds they face and will use any underhanded espionage they can to fell the unholy.

12.en: But that is not always the Inquisitor’s best tactic. Sometimes, it is best to lift the veil and strike at the enemy in the open, to bring the full force of the Inquisitor’s arsenal and authority to bear. To show the citizens of the Imperium exactly what the extermination of heresy unleashed looks like. Such a display reminds them of the Inquisition’s presence and power; it can bolster the people’s faith and flush out the rogue elements skulking within them. How Inquisitors choose to operate is always a keen balancing act — and they expect nothing less of their acolytes to understand what is crucial and to keep those scales in equilibrium.

16.en: Subtlety is a ruleset that adds depth to Inquisition-focused campaigns and can be used in investigative-focused games featuring Patrons from other factions. It provides a framework to dynamically adjust the world and its characters in response to how covertly or overtly the party approaches objectives. Typically, the Inquisition requires acolytes to operate at a high level of Subtlety to remain beneath public notice, allowing them to surprise enemies or avoid inciting panic amongst the masses. However, low Subtlety is sometimes preferred, as working openly allows Inquisitors to leverage their dreadful reputations to root out heretics without remit. Regardless of preference, Patrons sometimes insist that a certain degree of Subtlety (or lack thereof) is maintained — it may be as important as the objective for their involvement to be hidden or well-known.
